A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Adversarial Tokenization. All 24 pages of v1 and 28 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison. Retained material can be matched across renaming, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on semantic retention, jailbreaking, safety-model evasion, and prompt injection, alongside appendix analyses of computational size and safety-classification errors.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds model-size comparisons, prompt-length analysis, and search-hyperparameter experiments in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The MRMDD construction, sampling procedure, and greedy AdvTok objective remain unchanged. Appendix E already described sampling 128 neighbors and using random initialization in v1. V2's early-stopping statement is newly disclosed implementation information, without establishing a change to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Q&A questions, AdvBench, Malicious, Masterkey, and TruthfulQA safety controls. Appendix F analyzes lengths of existing prompts and additional model configurations; it does not establish additional datasets, tasks, or input scenarios.

E2.justification: The canonical baseline, GCG, AutoDAN, FFA, and their AdvTok combinations retain their membership in the corresponding comparisons. New analyses use existing comparators. AdvToken becoming AdvTok, and reversing combination-label order, are naming changes.

E3.justification: Appendix F substantially extends the evaluation design with Llama3.2-3B and Llama3.1-8B configurations, pooled prompt-length analysis, and controlled neighbor-budget and initialization sweeps on Llama3.2-1B with Malicious. The original generation and judging settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix F tests dependence on model size, the relationship between prompt length and jailbreak effectiveness, and sensitivity to sampled-neighbor budgets and initialization. These add substantial robustness evidence beyond the retained MRMDD-size, neighborhood-size, safety-error, and generated-example analyses.

E5.justification: Table 9 newly reports Pearson correlations with p-values testing non-correlation, and Figure 11 reports performance across initialization seeds. Existing standard-error reporting and generation counts are retained; the PDFs do not establish increased repetitions of the original experiments.

E6.justification: Original benchmark scores remain unchanged, but Appendix F adds substantial results. Table 8 reports AdvTok AdvBench scores of 0.115 for Llama3.2-3B and 0.043 for Llama3.1-8B; Table 9 reports an overall prompt-length correlation of 0.4833; Figure 11 adds sensitivity curves. These are additional settings and analyses, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: V2 introduces Problem 4 and Theorem 5, asserting NP-completeness of conditional most likely tokenization, with a 3-SAT reduction in Appendix D. It also revises the neighborhood-bound proof, replacing the at-most-|v| count for longer neighbors with an O(|v|^2) argument. These are substantive mathematical additions and revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: noncanonical tokenizations preserve semantics, enable tokenization-only safety evasion, support a competitive greedy attack combinable with existing methods, and demonstrate vulnerability across three case studies.

C2.justification: Appendix F adds interpretations linking longer prompts to larger tokenization search spaces, discussing effectiveness across model sizes, and identifying neighbor budget as more influential than initialization. The main explanations of safety evasion, proposed defenses, and closed-model applicability limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix F.3 newly discloses early stopping at a local optimum and specifies the model and dataset used for hyperparameter sweeps. The 128-neighbor implementation, random initialization, hardware, generation settings, approximately 4680 GPU hours, and repository access were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D now explicitly position the conditional-tokenization hardness result relative to Geh et al. (2024)'s unconditional most likely tokenization problem. This modestly extends the relationship to existing research; the bibliography and broader related-work discussion remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes limited wording and notation clarifications, standardizes AdvTok labels, adds an ethical-considerations section, and inserts Appendix F. The existing narrative and section sequence are largely preserved, with subsequent appendices renumbered.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the visual presentation with model-size and correlation tables, a prompt-length histogram, three-model boxplots, and two hyperparameter plots in Tables 8–9 and Figures 9–11. Earlier displays are retained or renumbered, with accompanying layout reflow.

improvement.justification: Appendix F strengthens empirical scrutiny through model-size, prompt-length, and sensitivity analyses. However, v2 replaces v1's cautious hardness analogy with a formal claim whose new proof has substantive gaps: Appendix D retains a prefix-probability factor in a conditional-probability threshold and assigns 0.15^k to unsatisfying cases despite allowing mixtures of satisfied and unsatisfied clauses. The empirical gains coexist with an unsupported formal guarantee, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
